Gain-of-function mutations in the same gene disrupt gap junction communication in keratinocytes, leading to palmoplantar keratoderma and alopecia. The convergence is on the shared pathway of gap junction communication, albeit in different cell types and with opposing functional consequences.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of any mutations in GJB2, GJB6, GJB3, or GJA1 in individuals with either disease, or the identification of entirely distinct causal pathways for each disease, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: A common pathogenic variant (AF > 0.01) in GJB2 associated with both conditions.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the opposing functional effects of GJB2 mutations in different cell types could inform targeted therapeutic strategies for both hearing loss and skin disorders. For instance, modulating gap junction activity could be explored for both conditions, but with opposite goals (enhancement vs. inhibition).
